diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..6abb6f4c20f9688573af7d0692a7e1686ecd1888 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -187,7 +187,8 @@ def humanize(word: str) -> str:
     """
     Capitalize the first word and turn underscores into spaces and strip a
     trailing ``"_id"``, if any. Like :func:`titleize`, this is meant for
-    creating pretty output.
+    creating pretty output, so words written in capitals, such as acronyms,
+    are kept as they are if the string also contains lowercase letters.
 
     Examples::
 
@@ -195,11 +196,21 @@ def humanize(word: str) -> str:
         'Employee salary'
         >>> humanize("author_id")
         'Author'
+        >>> humanize("NASA_rocket_launch")
+        'NASA rocket launch'
 
     """
+    keep_capitals = any(char.islower() for char in word)
+
+    def downcase(match: typing.Match[str]) -> str:
+        part = match.group(1)
+        if keep_capitals and len(part) > 1 and part.isupper():
+            return part
+        return part.lower()
+
     word = re.sub(r"_id$", "", word)
     word = word.replace('_', ' ')
-    word = re.sub(r"(?i)([a-z\d]*)", lambda m: m.group(1).lower(), word)
+    word = re.sub(r"(?i)([a-z\d]*)", downcase, word)
     word = re.sub(r"^\w", lambda m: m.group(0).upper(), word)
     return word
 
@@ -360,6 +371,9 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
     create a nicer looking title. :func:`titleize` is meant for creating pretty
     output.
 
+    Words written in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they are if the
+    string also contains lowercase letters.
+
     Examples::
 
       >>> titleize("man from the boondocks")
@@ -370,13 +384,40 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
 
     """
-    return re.sub(
-        r"\b('?\w)",
-        lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
-        humanize(underscore(word)).title()
-    )
+    if not any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        # There is no telling acronyms from other words in an all-caps string
+        # like "HELLO WORLD", so it is titleized as it always has been.
+        return re.sub(
+            r"\b('?\w)",
+            lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
+            humanize(underscore(word)).title()
+        )
+
+    def capitalize(match: typing.Match[str]) -> str:
+        apostrophe, part = match.groups()
+        # Keep words in capitals, like "NASA" or "DON'T", but not a capital
+        # after an apostrophe in a word that isn't, like "David'S".
+        if part.isupper() and (
+                not apostrophe or match.string[match.start() - 1].isupper()):
+            return match.group()
+        part = part.lower().title()
+        if apostrophe:
+            part = part[0].lower() + part[1:]
+        return apostrophe + part
+
+    # The same as humanize(underscore(word)), except that the case is kept
+    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = word.replace("-", "_")
+    word = re.sub(r"_[iI][dD]$", "", word)
+    word = word.replace("_", " ")
+    return re.sub(r"\b('?)(\w+)", capitalize, word)
